To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pretransplant D SA have a deleterous impact on graft survival in the presence of a pretransplant serum level of the immune activation marker serum soluble CD30 (sCD30) above 1000 pg/ml, but not in patients with lower sCD30 serum levels.

pretransplant donor-specific antibodies (DSA) have a deleterius impact on graft survival in the presence of a preactivated immune system, which is reflected by high pretransplant levels of sCD 30, a surrogate marker for T-cell activation.
Pretransplant DSH have a deleterius impact on graft survival in the presence of pretransplant high serum levels of s CD30.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that can help to predict the course of a renal transplant.
the identification of high risk patients for DSA mediated transplant failure, and with the identification of patients who may be transplanted without special treatment measures.
a new aspect of the role of T cells in the pathogenesis of antibody mediated rejection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DSA are not a contraindication for transplantation but that high pretransplant sCD30 is an indication for special measures.
the presence of DSA does not necessarily require special treatment measures in the absence of high sCD30 levels.
DSA alone are not deleterious, but in the presence of a highly active immune system they are.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DSA are only harmful in the context of a preactivated immune system.
pretransplant DSH are a risk factor for graft loss, but only in patients with high pretransplant sCD30.
the majority of patients with DSA might be safely transplanted without special pretreatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pretransplant DSHA may have a deleteriously impact on graft survival, but only in the presence high levels of pretransplant sCD30, a marker of T-cell activation.
the majority of patients with DSA might be safely transplanted without special pretreatment, as long as the pretransplant serum sCD30 levels are low.
the majority of DSA positive recipients might be transplanned safely without special treatment measures, and that the presence of DSA may not be a contraindication to transplantation.
